Welcome to The Bilingual Primary School
We are a pioneering state-funded primary school in the heart of Brighton and Hove where children learn through English and Spanish every day. Our unique admissions arrangements enable children from across the city (BN1, BN2, BN3 & BN41.) to join our school, regardless of how close they live. We have children from English speaking homes, Spanish speaking homes and homes where other languages are spoken - over 30 languages are currently spoken by families in our community!
All children are welcome here to learn across our broad, balanced curriculum which covers the content of the national curriculum with some content taught through each language. Children thrive in our innovative programme, developing global citizenship, enquiring minds and language skills. We hope you can find the information you are looking for on our website. If you have any further queries, please contact us at info@bilingualprimaryschool.org.uk.
The Love of Learning Through Language
Our vision for the Bilingual Primary School, Brighton & Hove, is to be at the leading edge of bilingual education in the UK
We aim to immerse children in a second language to stimulate and promote dual language communication, and in doing so enrich and expand their academic, cultural and social worlds.
Please click here to see our new propectus to find out more about the Bilingual Primary School!
Headteachers Welcome Message - English & Spanish
Dear Bilingual Primary School community
Welcome to our school!
I have been both grateful and honored to take on the role of headteacher at the Bilingual Primary School since September 2020. This year marks a new chapter in the school's development with an enhanced leadership structure giving capacity to further the school's vision.

Mathematics Curriculum Overview and Progression Document
Mastering Number Curriculum Overview and Progression Document
The National curriculum for mathematics aims to ensure that all pupils:
At the Bilingual Primary School, we aim to implement these requirements by teaching a mastery curriculum. The essential idea behind mastery is that all children need a deep understanding of the mathematics they are using so that future mathematical learning is built on solid foundations. We expect the majority of children to move through the maths curriculum at broadly the same pace; however, more time might be spent on a concept with children who are not ready to progress, while other children may grasp concepts more quickly and challenged with more sophisticated problems rather than moving them onto new content.
Become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics
Reason mathematically
Solve problems
FOUR KEY ASPECTS TO MATHEMATICAL MASTERY
This includes a belief that all pupils are capable of doing and understanding maths, given sufficient time. With good teaching, appropriate resources, effort and a ‘can do’ attitude, all children can enjoy and achieve in mathematics.
This offers one set of mathematical concepts and big ideas for all pupils. All children need access to these concepts and ideas and to the connections between them. Using manipulables and pictorial representations can be beneficial for helping children to master new concepts, and enable children who prefer a visual approach to learning to keep up with the class.
This involves keeping the class working together on the same topic, whilst at the same time addressing the need for all pupils to master the curriculum and for some to gain greater depth of proficiency and understanding. Challenge is provided by going deeper rather than accelerating into new mathematical content. More time is spent on teaching topics to allow for the development of depth and sufficient practice to embed learning.
Mastery is not just being able to memorise key facts and procedures and answer test questions accurately and quickly. It involves knowing ‘why’ as well as knowing ‘that’ and knowing ‘how’. It means being able to use knowledge appropriately, flexibly and creatively and to apply it in new and unfamiliar situations. Mastery of facts, procedures and concepts needs time to explore the concept in detail and time to allow for sufficient practice to develop fluency.
A mastery approach
A mastery curriculum
Teaching for mastery
WHITE ROSE MATHS
At BPS we use White Rose Maths (WRM) resources to support our delivery of our mastery curriculum and ensure coverage of the National Curriculum for mathematics. Parents can find support and resources using the following links to the WRM website. Please note that some ‘premium’ features are only available for access in school.

This APP is for children in EYFS and KS1 – it helps children build greater number confidence and fluency. It’s all about targeted practice in engaging, one-minute chunks!
WRM have teamed up with TV presenter, teacher and parent Michael Underwood to bring you a mini-series that explains how the children are taught mathematics topics at school.

Relationships & Sex Education (RSE)
WHY WE TEACH RELATIONSHIPS AND SEX EDUCATION
At our school, we use Brighton & Hove PSHE team resources to deliver an age appropriate Relationships and Sex education (RSE) curriculum with the aim of teaching the knowledge and skills to help our pupils to have happier, healthier, and safer lives, now and in the future.
We recognise how important families are in supporting children to understand and manage their changing bodies and their relationships with others as they grow from children to young adults.
We aim to work in partnership with families to provide all pupils with clear, factual information about how bodies work, how to manage their feelings and boost their self-esteem. RSE lessons provide a safe space to discuss and explore ideas, and the opportunity to practise the skills needed to navigate their friendships and to keep themselves safe.
At BPS, RSE is focused on friendships skills & healthy relationships, understanding puberty, families and people who care for us, and how to keep healthy and safe. In Y6, topics on grown up relationships, marriage and human reproduction are also covered.
Our RSE curriculum meets the requirements of the Department for Education Relationships, Sex and Health Education statutory Guidance and the Equalities Duties on Schools. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/relationships-sex-and-health-education-guides-for-schools
Since 2021, Relationships Education is statutory for all pupils, although parents & carers have the choice of withdrawing their child from the sex education element of these RSE units of learning (please refer to our PSHE policy for more details).
The sex education element of RSE covers how a baby starts from a sperm and an egg and basic information about human sexual reproduction. In the B&H RSE lessons, this is a small part of a lesson in Year 2, one lesson in Year 4 and one in Year 6.
Research suggests that RSE does not encourage sexual behaviour. Instead it is effective in preventing harmful or risky behaviours (UNESCO and Sex Education Forum 2022). https://www.unesco.org/en/health-education/cse-campaign
Safe Learning for All
All RSE lessons are taught by the class teacher, who creates a safe environment for learning with the use of ground rules, boundaries for asking questions, a variety of paired, group and whole class activities, and carefully chosen age appropriate picture books and videos.
Care is given to provide appropriate support for pupils with additional needs. If you feel that your child may find any particular content challenging, your child’s class teacher will work with you to order to ensure the learning environment and context is right for their stage of development and understanding.

What our pupils say about RSE at BPS:
‘It makes you feel safe and know you will make the right choices.’
‘The lessons made me feel less awkward.’
‘Using scientific language makes it easier and less people giggle!’
‘We talk about what we’ve done with our parents.’
By the end of primary school, the aim is that all B&H pupils have understood the following core messages to ensure they are prepared for their next stage of life at secondary school:
Core Messages for Y6 Pupils about Puberty and Relationships:
At this age, some of you might start feeling attracted to or fancy people but some of you might not.
There is no set time for these feeling to start, so don’t worry if you don’t have these feelings.
How you feel about yourself, and your identity and your relationships may change at this time or in the future.
You have a right to be who you want to be and not to be restricted by gender stereotypes.
3. Accept your changing body
Bodies develop at different speeds and into all different shapes and sizes, not just the ones you see in the media.
You have the right to ask questions and get support with these changes.
Friendships should be fun!
If friends don’t make you feel good about being yourself, then are they good friends?
You are the boss of your body; you have the right to say if you don’t like how you are being touched.
Pay attention to your early warning signs and talk to a trusted person if you feel at all uncomfortable.
6. Know Your Feelings
Puberty can be a very confusing time where you might find your mood changing often and you might have more extreme feelings about yourself and others.
Try and name your feelings and know that all feelings are ok, it is what you decide to do about them that matters.
Think about what you share with others and telling or keeping secrets.
Notice your early warning signs and act on them!
Keep talking to your friends and family and ask questions when you need to.
There’s nothing so awful (or too small) to talk to someone about.
Remember there are people around you (parents, carers, trusted adults, teachers, mentors, ChildLine) you can get help and advice from if you’re faced with tricky decisions or situations or just need someone to talk to.
Top tips for talking to your child about bodies, growing up, relationships and sex
Suggested resources to support you in having these conversations:
NSPCC advice for talking about difficult topics with your child https://www.nspcc.org.uk/keeping-children-safe/support-for-parents/talking-about-difficult-topics/
Puberty – Childline https://www.childline.org.uk/info-advice/you-your-body/puberty/
Working together
The best learning occurs with partnership with pupil, parents and carers and the school. We hope that by sharing our RSE curriculum with families (more details on the website) you will be able to build on the conversations and learning at home to ensure your child has the knowledge and skills needed to be safe, have positive relationships and be confident to be themselves as they grow and change.
Please contact your child’s class teacher or our PSHE coordinator, Nick Keyworth, if you want to find out more or discuss any aspect of the statutory RSE at our school.

At the Bilingual Primary School, we have a balanced immersion programme where English and Spanish are valued equally throughout the day. We teach Spanish literacy daily as well as teaching Art, DT, History, Geography, Computing, Music, Science and PE through Spanish.
Children at BPS are immersed in Spanish language throughout the day in their class and around the school. Our bilingual teaching assistants (TAs) speak to the children in Spanish, except when explaining English or maths work. All teachers speak Spanish as much as possible around the school - especially for organisational language in the classroom. Children respond in Spanish wherever possible and are encouraged to ask questions in Spanish.
Year 2 – Science - How animals are adapted to their habitats
Each year group has a Specialist Bilingual Teaching Assistant (SBTA) who teaches five Spanish literacy lessons per week. Our exciting curriculum supports children to learn new Spanish vocabulary and practise grammar through a wide range of engaging activities, such as games, role-plays and presentations. Children also have the opportunity to write in different genres and read both fiction and non-fiction texts.
Year 4 – The Egyptians
We use teacher assessment to measure progress and report attainment to parents. We look at the four language skills of speaking, reading, listening and writing. Our assessment system is linked to the Common European Framework (CEFR) to support assessment in year 6.
Year 6 - The Causes and Consequences of climate change

Booking Procedure and Policy
After school club starts when your child finishes school, we collect them from their classroom and take them into the big and small halls where they first sit to enjoy a fruit snack provided by us or their own lunchbox snacks while they catch up with friends. We offer two sessions: early (until 5pm) and late (until 6pm) and always hold some spaces for ad hoc bookings for those days where you just need a bit of extra time, as well as extensions if you’re booked for an early session but can’t make it on time!
Once the rest of the school leaves and the front gates are closed, LingoClub properly starts! Children can play freely outside, football, ping pong, running around having fun with our hula hoops, or creating their own world in our big playground. We encourage children to go outside in all weather and they love the fresh air.
Inside, we have at least four stations, where children can join our daily, staffed arts and crafts activity, play with lego, play interactive board and card games, or play freely with their friends.
We also have a Play Zone - this is just for our reception children. Although children in reception can use everywhere in the club, and they do, they also have this space just for them which is full of toys for them to play with if they need a bit of down time after their day at school. There is always a dedicated member of staff based at our Play Zone.
We also offer an exciting timetable of extra-curricular clubs which run alongside our main provision. These clubs are run in smaller groups with dedicated staff and are more structured than our main club. We charge a small additional fee for these clubs. The timetable for next term’s extra-curricular clubs can be found below.
LingoClub is a fun, friendly, immersive Spanish setting, with a team of long-standing Spanish speaking staff who get to know your children and plan activities to nurture their interests, all around learning Spanish.
Extra-Curricular Clubs:
About our Extra-Curricular Clubs
Extra-curricular clubs cost £2.50 in addition to your main LingoClub fee. The sessions are run in smaller groups, are more structured and are run by dedicated club staff. Here’s what you can expect:
Scooter club is a chance for all of our children to let off some steam on wheels! We provide helmets, protective pads and scooters, so don’t worry about providing your own. We use a one-way ‘rink’ system and also have ramps so the children can try out some stunts!
A new club for September 2026 and run by our very own artist Rebecca. Art club is a focused art session, using a variety of media in a vibrant, multi-sensory creative hub designed to build confidence, fine motor skills, and self-expression through hands-on exploration.
New for September and run by a familiar face at BPS! Joana will be running an exciting, friendly and interactive Portuguese club each week, focusing on different areas of vocabulary and culture across the Portuguese-speaking world. All levels are welcome, Joana will ensure every child is catered for.
Our wonderful team member Domi plans and runs Creative Club, where the children do a different creative craft activity each week. These sessions guide and nurture children’s creativity and provide a calm space for children to grow and hone their creative skills. Domi’s sessions are usually fully booked, so book early to avoid disappointment!
Run by our local, professional football coach, Luca Slaney, our football sessions are structured and based on skills. Luca is a fantastic coach who inspires the children and plans really fun and engaging sessions. His clubs are often fully booked, so book your place early to avoid disappointment! This year we have split the sessions into boys on Tuesdays and girls on Fridays.
Commercial dance is energetic, dynamic, and often combines different dance styles like hip-hop, jazz, and street dance. Our wonderful I-Star coach runs this dance class, helping children to build their strength, confidence and dance skills!
Lego club is a hive of activity every week! Run by our resident lego-enthusiast Luke, children are given lego kits with instructions and can build their own kit or work with friends! Children can choose from a huge variety of kits from Disney to Star Wars as well as traditional construction sets. We encourage the children to take care of their kits and take pride in their creations and this is a very popular club!
Chess club, run by BPS parent Steven, is a great way for children to learn the strategic skills of chess with friends. We provide players an opportunity to play casually, socialize, and even participate in small tournaments.
Our Wednesday music sessions are run by Pedro, parent at BPS and amazing guitar teacher. Pedro’s calm and nurturing personality really drives the children to learn from him. During this session for our younger LingoClubbers, there is a variety of instruments for children to experiment with, including percussion, guitars, xylophones and more, and Pedro guides children through timing and melodies to create wonderful sounds with the club members!
Also run by Pedro, the children can either bring their own guitar, or they can use one of ours (please let us know if you need one). They learn to play chords and notes and learn to play individually but also how to work together as a group.
Run by our very own Marine Biologist Vivi, this is one of our newest clubs. Vivi shares her passion for the environment with our growing group of environmentalists, by sharing ways to reduce waste, recycle rubbish into beautiful things and to learn some Spanish terms that are used when we talk about the environment too. This group is usually run outdoors.
Our gymnastics sessions are run by two coaches from the amazing I-Star academy. Our enthusiastic coaches really drive the children to learn from them and these sessions are friendly and inclusive. Children will learn and improve their gymnastics skills each week with a session on Wednesday and Thursday.
Our professional coach Luca runs netball at BPS. An extremely popular and growing group, these sessions focus on a mixture of skills and tactics, and usually culminate in a great game of netball.
Run by the lovely Clare, a professional swimwear designer and BPS mum, our sewing club is small but mighty! Children learn sewing skills and make incredible creations over the weeks, which involve different needle and sewing skills. This group has a very limited capacity, so book early to avoid disappointment.
Open to all year groups, our coach Luca runs multi-sports. Luca focusses on a new sport each week, running mini-skills sessions and giving children an idea of all the amazing sports out there. He runs sessions on mainstream sports, but also some of the lesser known ones. Our active children absolutely love Luca’s sessions.
Run by Ednardo, our Capoeira club is very popular with the children and returning for September 2026. Capoeira is a Brazilian martial art, dance, and cultural expression that combines elements of dance, acrobatics, music, and combat techniques. The children absolutely love learning to express themselves to music in Ednardo’s sessions.
New for September and run by a familiar face at BPS! Joana will run this club for our readers at LingoClub. Each half term, we will ask you to buy the book we'll be reading. Each session will involve reading part of the book followed by a lovely, hands on activity. With this club, we hope to inspire reluctant readers and enrich enthusiastic ones by exploring new worlds through stories! Our first book will be Captain Sunshine by Alex Milway. We will invoice parents for the cost of the book and keep the copies at school for the half term. Afterwards, children will be able to take their copies home with them.
Open to Reception and Year 1 only, this is one of our newest clubs and an opportunity for our youngest children to move, swing, balance and roll across our gymnastics equipment! This session is unstructured but supervised, and we set up a short course using PE equipment and cover the floor in soft mats so that children can test their agility skills and are encouraged to follow the course.
New for September 2026, Wellbeing club is run by Lucy from Ethereal Flow Kids. Each week will combine breathwork, mindfulness, storytelling, creative activities, nature connection, and practical wellbeing tools in a fun, engaging, and nurturing environment. Accessible for all children to help them build confidence, self-awareness, emotional regulation skills, resilience, and positive mental wellbeing.
How to Book a place at LingoClub:
If you have never used LingoClub before, you will need to create a profile on Magic Booking.
Once you have done this, you’ll be able to make and manage your bookings 24/7. Bookings are made on a half-termly basis, if you require last minute wraparound care or a bit more flexibility week-by-week we offer ad-hoc bookings.
You will need to re-book your sessions each half term, and we will email you to notify you that bookings are open.
You can arrive any time before your session ends and ring our doorbell to collect your child early but we do operate a strict late fee for any parents who are late to collect their child. This enables us to keep our normal club prices as low as possible. Places at LingoClub are non-transferable and non-refundable. This includes sessions missed for illness, appointments and school trips. We staff and resource all of our clubs based on the number of bookings we have, so it is impossible for us to refund missed sessions while maintaining a competitive price. Thank you for your understanding on this.
If you have any queries about the booking process, please see our bookings policy.

If you are interested in place for your child in Reception next school year, see our admissions page for more information
Educational Visits Programme
At BPS, our Educational Visits Programme is carefully planned to broaden and enhance both the learning and social experience of our pupils. School visits enable children to get out into the world around them and experience it first-hand, helping children to develop their risk awareness and preparing them for the next steps in their education. Every visit has a clear learning objective and is closely linked to the curriculum and learning surrounding that particular topic. Our aim is for children to gain a great deal from these visits, including collaborative skills, independence and, especially for the younger ones, the confidence to venture out into the world without parents/carers. Children in Year 6 also get the chance to take part in a residential visit, which for some is their first experience of being away from home. Our Educational Visits Programme then culminates in a 5-day trip to Madrid, where our Year Six children get the opportunity to apply their Spanish learning in meaningful and purposeful contexts, whilst also getting the chance to visit one of our partner schools to experience a day at a Spanish school.
Here is a list of the visits planned for this academic year:
Alongside school trips, we also enhance our curriculum through inviting a broad range of guest visitors into BPS. This can take different forms, such as in-person assemblies, online assemblies, interactive workshops or interviews. For example, in the past year, we have had multiple author visits, flamenco workshops, Herstmonceux Planetarium, Zoo Lab, different local religious leaders, to name just a few of the visitors coming into school.
Performances and Sporting Events Programme
Alongside our Educational Visits, at BPS, we ensure children have the opportunity to partake in a range of different experiences that extend beyond the academic. Our Performances and Sporting Events Programme is designed to build year-on-year, providing different contexts for children to develop resilience, confidence, team work and independence. Our aim is that that our performances showcase the bilingual learning that takes plce at BPS.
